subject.title: [Feature Request]: Multi-lane concurrency support for sub-agents via sessions_spawn

question: Should `sessions_spawn` select only operator-declared lane ids under an aggregate sub-agent cap, allow arbitrary caller-created lanes, or retain one global pool?
rationale: The lane id would be model-facing resource-policy input; its trust model, configuration precedence, and total concurrency budget determine whether callers can bypass operator limits.

options.title: Declared lanes plus aggregate cap
options.body: Allow only configured lane ids, preserve `subagent` as the default, and enforce both per-lane and total sub-agent limits.

options.title: Arbitrary dynamic lanes
options.body: Accept caller-selected lane strings with defaults, gaining flexibility but increasing resource-bypass and configuration-drift risk.

options.title: Keep one global lane
options.body: Retain the current pool and address fairness through per-agent caps or queue policy instead of new lane identities.

recommendation.title: Declared lanes plus aggregate cap
recommendation.body: Allow only configured lane ids, preserve `subagent` as the default, and enforce both per-lane and total sub-agent limits.

likelyOwner.reason: The history ties this person most directly to the original spawn tool, concurrency resolver, and current product-contract discussion.
